stories.title: Rail companies sued for £5m over oil spill caused by derailment
stories.summary: Network Rail is suing two rail companies for more than £5m after a fuel spill caused by a train derailment threatened an "environmental disaster" at a designated site for protection. The body filed a legal claim earlier this month against DB Cargo UK and Touax Rail over the derailment near Llangennech, Carmarthenshire, in August 2020. The incident saw 10 wagons of the 25-wagon train derail, causing 446,000 litres of fuel to spill, and about 300 people had to leave the area due to the blaze. In High Court documents, Network Rail claimed that the derailment occurred because the wagon had "not been maintained with reasonable care" and is seeking damages for negligence. No one was injured, but 116,000 litres of fuel ignited while 330,000 litres drained into surrounding wetlands, which form part of a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Special Area of Conservation. The Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) concluded in January 2022 that the derailment was caused by a set of wheels on one of the wagons locking, likely the result of a brake defect after "inadequate maintenance practices" were found in the investigation. Network Rail, which owns, operates, maintains and develops Britain's railways, claimed that the derailment occurred because the wagon had "not been maintained with reasonable care" by Touax. It is also seeking damages from DB Cargo UK, claiming that the latter "breached a contractual duty to ensure that reasonable care was taken" in maintaining the wagon. Lawyers for the body said it expected to recover "more than £5m" with DB Cargo and Touax yet to file defences. A hearing in the case is due to take place. The locomotive was pulling the wagons from Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire, to Theale, near Reading, when the derailment occurred. The line was closed for six months after the incident and did not fully reopen for almost a year, with 30,000 tonnes of fuel-soaked soil having to be excavated.

stories.title: Russia, India discuss cooperation in manned spaceflight — Manturov
stories.summary: The Russian first deputy prime minister added that Russia and India are discussing potential cooperation in civil aircraft manufacturing
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.

Russia and India are discussing cooperation in the space sector, including manned spaceflights, Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov said at a meeting of the two countries’ intergovernmental commission on cooperation.
"Our countries continue their dialogue in the space sector.
There is broad scope for cooperation here, including manned spaceflights, rocket engine development, and satellite navigation," he said.
Manturov added that Russia and India are discussing potential cooperation in civil aircraft manufacturing.
There is strong interest in Russian civilian aircraft in India, he said.

stories.title: Kenya: Designer turns to traditional clothesmaking methods
stories.summary: Mass production is quickly changing the fashion industry, with environmentalists warning about the impact on the planet. However in Nairobi, one young designer is refusing to follow current production trends - instead, he’s turning back to a traditional craft. The founder of Mukabwa studios, Hillary Mukubwa uses hand looms to create clothes and fabrics. He says he feels like an anomaly in going back to old traditions, stating, "modernisation kills the aspect of traditional craftsmen and ways of doing work. So, being a young guy, it is a bit not normal to go back. But I just wanted to be that person who kind of tries to revive the old practices, because this is where culture lives.'' He views the hand looms as a way of keeping Kenya's cultural heritage alive. "The difference between the hand looms and the electric machines is that these hand looms, first of all, they are traditional. So, you find that they carry a story. It's a piece of art, you know. Rather than producing masses, they produce with meaning,'' he explains. Clients say they find the clothes more interesting than what's available on the high street due to their individality.

stories.title: Russian banks’ net profit rises 18% in July to $5.28 bln — Bank of Russia
stories.summary: Expenses declined mainly in the corporate segment by 77%
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.
The Russian banking sector’s net profit rose by 18% in July 2026 compared with June, reaching 443 bln rubles ($5.28 bln), according to materials from the Bank of Russia.
"The sector’s net profit increased to 443 bln rubles in July, up 68 bln rubles, or 18%, from June.
Annualized return on equity rose to around 24% from around 20%.
Core profit amounted to 442 bln rubles, up 98 bln rubles, or 28%, amid a decline in provisions for problem assets to 168 bln rubles from 282 bln rubles in June, a decrease of 114 bln rubles, or 40%.
Expenses declined mainly in the corporate segment, by 103 bln rubles, or 77%," the regulator said.
The Bank of Russia noted that some banks released provisions, including after certain borrowers updated their business plans to reflect higher revenues.
Meanwhile, non-core income declined by 46 bln rubles ($549 mln), or 31%, primarily due to lower dividend income from subsidiaries and affiliated companies.
In May, the Bank of Russia raised its forecast for banks’ net profit in 2026 to 3.4-3.9 trillion rubles ($40.55-46.51 bln) from 3.3-3.8 trillion rubles ($39.36-45.32 bln).
The regulator later said it could raise the forecast further.

stories.title: Russian household bank funds rise by 0.3% in July amid high demand for cash
stories.summary: On an annual basis, household funds held in banks increased by 9.5% in July, reaching $815.74 bln
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.
Household funds held in Russian banks edged up by 0.3%, or 0.2 trillion rubles ($2.39 bln), in July compared with June amid high demand for cash, according to materials from the Bank of Russia.
"Household funds increased by 0.2 trillion rubles in July (+0.3%, the same as in June).

This moderate growth may be associated with increased consumer activity and persistently high demand for cash (the amount of cash in circulation rose by 0.7 trillion rubles in July after increasing by 0.5 trillion rubles in June)," the regulator noted.
On an annual basis, household funds held in banks increased by 9.5% in July, reaching 68.4 trillion rubles ($815.74 bln).
Funds held by legal entities in banks increased by 0.4 trillion rubles ($4.77 bln), or 0.6%, in July after declining by 0.01% in June, despite substantial dividend payments.
According to the Bank of Russia, the increase was driven primarily by exporting companies.

Funds held in escrow accounts declined by 60 bln rubles ($716 mln) in July, or 0.8%, after rising by 1.2% in June: the volume of escrow account releases increased, while mortgage lending cooled somewhat.
